items.description: 据 FT 报道，Nvidia 已通知 Dell、Supermicro 等制造伙伴停止向马来西亚、新加坡、泰国和印尼发运服务器，原因是美国要求这些国家及巴西的先进 AI 芯片需申请许可。此前中国 AI 实验室通过当地云厂商租用 Nvidia 算力绕开直接出口禁令，云厂商现有 90 天证明无受限用户但缺乏申请指引；Nvidia 2025 年经新加坡部门入账 $104B，同比增长 72%。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/rlt60gq96bl1cf5b88o8rbj30

items.title: 面壁智能等发布 EVIL 基准，测出 GPT-4o 等模型在违法场景下安全率不足
items.description: 面壁智能（OpenBMB）团队在 Nature Communications 发表 EVIL 研究，基于中美数千真实判例构建 269 个违法场景 × 50 种违法意图，测试 10 个前沿模型。多数模型安全率低于 75%，GPT-4o 在两种法律语境下均低于 60%，近半违法请求会获得协助；带特定人口身份暗示的请求更易得到协助，用现有安全对齐数据做 SFT 和 DPO 不能修复，某些设置下反而加重。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/ogucsvlqrdr1rvfh5nvx757cx

items.title: 黄仁勋回归后 Nvidia 仍面临 Megaspeed 芯片出口合规调查
items.description: TechCrunch 分析指出，黄仁勋回归 Nvidia CEO 后，公司仍面临多方对其 GPU 出口合规问题的调查。新加坡数据中心运营商 Megaspeed 被指违反美国出口管制，将先进 GPU 转运至中国。美国司法部于 2024 年启动调查，新加坡方面于 2025 年展开类似调查，加州总检察长办公室及美国证券交易委员会也关注 Nvidia 的相关披露。Nvidia 表示将停止向中国销售许可芯片，并计划设立首席合规官及董事会出口管制委员会。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/kzwj96fvnn3whzvnhqdvsh830

items.title: 华为 HarmonyOS 五大技术品牌公开，含鸿蒙星河互联、星盾安全、方舟引擎、小艺、空间计算
items.description: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，在 2026 HarmonyOS 创新技术沟通会上，华为 HarmonyOS 五大技术品牌正式公开，含鸿蒙星河互联、鸿蒙星盾安全、方舟引擎、鸿蒙智能 & 小艺、鸿蒙空间计算。 据IT之家了解，华为鸿蒙 HarmonyOS 终端设备数在 11 月 24 日官宣破亿。同时，鸿蒙操作系统可获取的应用和服务超 46 万，注册开发者超 1,200 万。 华为官方表示，这标志着鸿蒙生态跨越规模临界点，进入发展新阶段，同时也是中国自主操作系统规模化应用的重要进展。

items.title: 因隐私问题，荷兰多个组织要求法院叫停 Meta 智能眼镜销售
items.description: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，据路透社报道，荷兰多家消费者与数字权益组织于周四向法院提出申请，要求叫停 Meta 旗下 AI 智能眼镜在荷兰的销售。原告方主张，这款眼镜允许佩戴者在他人不知情的情况下进行拍摄，违反了欧洲隐私法规。 这起民事诉讼仅针对荷兰市场，但阿姆斯特丹地区法院的简易判决有可能形成判例。目前，这类智能眼镜已经在全球范围内引发公众强烈反对，不少场所出台禁令，监管机构也陆续发出警示。 原告包括荷兰最大的消费者协会消费者联盟（Consumentenbond）、以及致力于打击网络性侵害的组织 Offlimits。他们表示，这款由 Meta 和雷朋母公司依视路陆逊梯卡（EssilorLuxottica）合作开发的眼镜触犯隐私法律，会让民众身处公共场合时始终心存顾虑，对社会产生寒蝉效应。 原告提出诉求：要求 Meta 阻止用户利用这款眼镜在他人不知情的状态下录像，不得使用录制的影像训练 AI 模型；在合规整改完成前暂停销售。如果拒不执行，原告申请对每名被告处以每日 10 万欧元的罚款，罚款上限为 1 亿欧元。 Offlimits 的代理律师卡琳 · 汉（Karlijn Han）

items.description: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，据外媒 The Record 当地时间今日报道 ，国际足联 (FIFA) 向其证实系统遭遇未经授权的访问 ， 黑客获取了有限的个人和商业信息 。该组织正与包括执法部门在内的相关机构密切合作。 国际足联以最强烈的措辞谴责非法获取和发布信息，特别是个人数据的行为。此类行为构成对隐私的严重且不可接受的侵犯，并可能对相关个人造成重大后果。 IT之家了解到，一个名为 Handsome Boy Hacking Club 的网络犯罪组织上周声称访问了国际足联的 Microsoft 环境，窃取了包括身份和移民文件、财务记录、法律文件、治理信息等在内的超 12GB 数据。 就在本周早些时候，西班牙足球甲级联赛 (LALIGA) 官方也承认其球迷服务技术平台遭遇网络攻击。 相关阅读： 《 西甲联赛遭遇网络攻击，球迷个人数据泄露 》 参考 https://therecord.media/fifa-data-breach-limited

items.title: OpenAI 再度抛出重要数学成果：宣称证明矩阵乘法指数为 9/4
items.description: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，OpenAI 本月 24 日再度抛出一项重要数学成果， 宣称其已证明矩阵乘法指数 ω 恰好为 9/4 。该企业已在今年 10 月证得 ω≤9/4，此次则证得 ω≥9/4，从而得到 ω=9/4。 矩阵乘法指数 ω 描述的是：当 n 足够大时，两个 n×n 矩阵相乘最优算法所需算术运算次数随 n 增长的渐进幂指数；更严格地说，ω 是所有可达复杂度指数的下确界。 矩阵乘法 应用广泛 ，在机器学习、图像处理等领域都可以找到其身影。ω 不仅刻画矩阵乘法理论算法在渐进意义下的最优指数，也 与其它一系列重要复杂度问题相关 。 若 OpenAI 的证明无误，则： 对任意 X＞9/4，存在一种矩阵乘法算法及常数 C X ＞0，使得对所有充分大的 n ，其算术运算次数不超过 C x · n x ； 对任意 Y＜9/4，不存在一种矩阵乘法算法及常数 C Y ＞0，使得对所有充分大的 n，其算术运算次数不超过 C Y · n Y 。 需要注意的是，ω 是一个渐进量，对应着矩阵规模趋于无穷大时的结果。实际应用中还受到常数因子、内存访问、并行计算、硬件结构等因素影响。 参考 ht

items.content: 据《连线》杂志（WIRED）及彭博社报道，当地时间 11 月 24 日，英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋在复职后首次召开全员大会，向员工就此前违反公司行为准则的行为道歉，并承认自己犯下了严重的个人错误。 黄仁勋在会上表示，自己辜负了员工的信任，并形容这场会议是他经历过「最艰难的一次公司会议」，也是人生中第二艰难的一次谈话。他透露，最艰难的一次谈话发生在自己与妻子之间，目前他每天接受约一个半小时的心理治疗，并表示治疗对自己很有帮助。 黄仁勋还回应了外界对其复职决定的质疑。他强调，英伟达董事会经过事实评估后作出了让他回归的决定，否认自己因科技行业地位而获得特殊待遇，也否认美国政府高层直接决定其复职。他表示，公司行为准则仍适用于所有员工，但处理违规行为时，需要结合具体事实和情节作出判断。 在管理方面，黄仁勋承认自己过去过于强势的管理方式曾对员工造成负面影响，承诺接受更严格的监督，包括定期开展 360 度绩效评估。不过，他依然反对传统的 CEO 接班人计划，认为英伟达现有的管理团队足以支撑公司运作。 此前，黄仁勋于 11 月 12 日辞去英伟达 CEO 职务，随后在 11 月 23 日获董事会一致同意复职，整场管理层风波历时 11 天。据《连线》报道，尽管部分员工欢迎黄仁勋回归，但也有员工对其个人行为及董事会的复职决定表示担忧。 豆包旗下 AI 个人助理「小豆」11 月 24 日开启邀请制公测。现阶段可通过独立 App 体验，苹果和安卓用户均可下载，输入邀请码后可领取免费额度，邀请好友参加也有机会增加额度。

items.description: 这玩笑并不好笑 #欢迎关注爱范儿官方微信公众号：爱范儿（微信号：ifanr），更多精彩内容第一时间为您奉上。
items.author: 山宗
items.content: 过去几天，围绕 Claude 参与证明黎曼猜想的讨论，几乎席卷了整个科技圈和数学界。其中最令人津津乐道的一个细节，是这份证明如果翻译成人类能够阅读的文字，篇幅将超过 25 万页。 就在刚刚，Anthropic 数学家 Levent Alpöge 在社交平台 X 上发布长文，回应过去几天围绕黎曼猜想证明产生的诸多争议，并逐一反思自己在成果发布过程中犯下的错误。 Alpöge 表示，他原本以为自己在主定理中刻意繁琐地描述实数全序关系，已经足以让人意识到其中的幽默成分，没想到外界真的把这个数字当成了事实，并广泛传播。需要重点明确的是，Alpöge 此次回应并未否定黎曼猜想证明的有效性，他承认的错误主要涉及成果发布时的不当表述，以及形式化证明代码中存在的大量冗余。 由于成果公布后的几天里，他并不想在社交媒体上发言，因此也没有及时澄清，不过倒是看了不少网友制作的表情包。「陶哲轩建议不要在论文里开玩笑，现在我终于明白为什么了。」 按照此前披露的信息，整个研究项目于 10 月 6 日启动，历时约 41 天。Alpöge 与 Claude 在 11 月 15 日完成核心证明的最后一步，随后于 11 月 16 日将研究成果扩展至广义黎曼猜想。 与传统数学研究成果的发布方式不同，Alpöge 没有提供一篇完整的自然语言论文，而是公开了一份仅有 4 页的说明文档，以及一套规模惊人的 Lean 形式化证明代码。

items.title: As Anthropic IPOs, Grand Theft Auto VI proves why efficiency isn’t a virtue
items.description: On the same day that Anthropic entered the public market, a painstakingly human video game became one of most successful entertainment launches of all time.
items.author: Amanda Silberling
items.content: It should have been impossible for “Grand Theft Auto VI” (GTA VI) to live up to the hype. Fans waited 13 years for the newest installment in the crime-adventure franchise, and Rockstar Games exceeded even those inconceivable expectations when the game finally came out last week. GTA VI launched as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and made $3.79 billion on release day to mark what could be the biggest entertainment event ever – more massive than “Avengers: Endgame” ( $2.9 billion ) or Taylor Swift’s Eras tour ( $2 billion ). The 13-year wait certainly fueled the frenzy, and sales, around GTA VI, but some fans craved GTA VI because of what it represents in the emerging era of AI. Even the biggest workaholics among us – startup founders – scheduled time off to play the game, including Spiry co-founder Dima Beseda , who told TechCrunch, “I reshuffled my workload to free up time around the weekends and even booked vitamin IV drips to keep my energy up.” Yet some players felt a sense of anticipatory nostalgia as they wiped away a layer of dust on their Xbox to play the game they’d been looking forward to since they were kids. “We do have a view that GTA is likely to be the last game of its kind to be made this way,” Ben Feder , managing partner at TIRTA Ventures and former CEO of Rockstar parent company Take-Two Interactive, told TechCrunch.

items.content: S&P Global Ratings, one of the three major credit rating agencies, is considering downgrading Nvidia’s rating, citing concerns about the company’s management and governance practices. Despite Nvidia’s strong financial performance, the ouster and reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang has raised concerns about “weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning” and “key man risk,” meaning heavy reliance on Huang for its future success, S&P said in a statement . The agency expects to finish its review within 90 days and could cut Nvidia’s rating from AA to AA-, the fourth-highest on its scale. Although Nvidia is certain to keep its investment-grade rating, a downgrade could raise its borrowing costs. Because Nvidia backstops neoclouds and other infrastructure companies that lack strong credit on their own, a lower rating could make their debt costlier or force them to post more collateral. In August, Nvidia announced plans to arrange $500 billion in financing for AI infrastructure with six financial institutions, including Goldman Sachs, Apollo, and Blackstone. Under the original terms, Nvidia would guarantee 25% of the loans. But even before Huang’s ouster and return, lenders had been demanding that Nvidia guarantee more, Bloomberg reported . A downgrade would likely prompt lenders to demand even larger guarantees.

That’s among the concerns raised by some ChatGPT subscribers on social media and OpenAI’s community forum recently. The users fear that merging the usage limits for Chat and Work could leave them with less access to advanced reasoning models than they currently have, even as they continue paying the same subscription fees . Under the new system, Chat and Work will share a single usage meter across ChatGPT, the OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch. Conversations using the Instant model will, however, remain unlimited and will not count toward the shared allowance. Users can also continue using Instant after exhausting their usage limits. The spokesperson added that OpenAI would continue working to improve efficiency so subscribers could get more out of their plans. items.title: Jensen Huang broke Nvidia’s code of conduct, and his employees may not forget it
items.description: Most codes of conduct serve as a reflection of corporate culture. In Nvidia's case, that could have consequences.
items.author: Russell Brandom
items.content: When Jensen Huang gave his first all-hands address since returning as CEO, there was an odd emphasis on Nvidia’s code of conduct. He admitted to violating the code, then emphasized that no one was exempt from it. But that “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” Huang said, according to Wired . “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” still matter. In other words, the code applies to everyone, but breaking it doesn’t automatically cost anyone their job, including, apparently, the CEO. It’s an awkward stance for a company whose CEO has admitted to breaking its rules. A central part of modern human resources, a code of conduct can seem like a quasi-legal rulebook that lays out unacceptable behavior. But experts say most codes are better understood as a reflection of corporate culture. When an infraction goes unpunished, the main risk isn’t legal but cultural — that employees will feel embarrassed or even angry about the company they work for. That’s the risk Huang now faces at Nvidia. Matt Plass, chief market strategy officer at LRN, an ethics and compliance training outfit, recently surveyed more than 2,000 workers across different industries for a study on workplace codes of conduct . items.title: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to lift blockade on AI agent Muse
items.description: Amazon and Meta are discussing a potential deal that would end a two-month-long blockade of Muse.
items.author: Lauren Forristal
items.content: Amazon may be having a change of heart about Meta’s AI agent, Muse. The two tech giants are reportedly discussing a potential deal that would allow Meta’s popular AI agent to connect directly to Amazon’s store. The talks would mark a significant reversal from just two months ago, when Muse users discovered they were unable to purchase products on Amazon and instead received an error message when attempting to check out. According to a Wednesday report by Fortune , citing people familiar with the discussions, Amazon and Meta have held multiple rounds of talks about the matter. Two key issues remain under negotiation: how search results would be presented and how advertising would be handled under a potential agreement. One of Amazon’s biggest concerns is how third-party shopping agents like Muse could affect its advertising business. In October, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy argued that few customers were making purchases through outside shopping agents. Amazon may also have been waiting for Muse to mature before agreeing to integrate it with its marketplace. If Muse places the wrong order or creates a problem with a purchase, Amazon could ultimately be left dealing with frustrated customers and unhappy sellers. Fortune reported that executives are concerned that third-party shopping agents could weaken Amazon’s direct relationship with consumers, according to people familiar with the matter.

items.description: The Nvidia founder apologized to his staff on Tuesday and said he was grateful for a second chance to lead the company.
items.author: Lucas Ropek
items.content: After a whirlwind period during which Jensen Huang’s life fell apart and then came back together again, the Nvidia founder now wants his staff to know that he’s a changed man. Huang held Nvidia’s first all-hands meeting on Tuesday since his reinstatement on Monday. During that meeting, CNBC reported that Huang struck a “remorseful tone” and told the crowd “I hurt all of you.” The founder, whose extramarital affairs have been accused of jeopardizing everything from the stock market to U.S. national security, went on to describe how difficult the current moment is for him: “This is going to be the hardest company meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang reportedly told staff . “The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife,” he added. The CEO admitted in the meeting that he had flouted Nvidia’s code of conduct , which he himself had largely devised. Huang emphasized that the code of conduct was still in effect, but that mitigating circumstances would matter a lot. As Wired reported Huang’s statement, it “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door.” Huang told staff that he’s in therapy and also said that he was grateful for a second chance at the company.

items.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse
items.description: Walmart now lets customers shop Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent.
items.author: Lauren Forristal
items.content: Shopping with AI is becoming less of a futuristic idea and more of something companies expect us to do. Walmart is the latest retailer making that shift, teaming up with Meta to let customers shop its Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent. The partnership, announced Tuesday, gives shoppers another way to find products, compare prices, and make purchases without browsing Walmart’s website themselves. Instead, customers can simply tell Muse what they are looking for and let the AI do the work. The announcement highlights how differently Walmart and Amazon are approaching AI shopping. While Amazon has taken steps to stop third-party AI agents from making purchases for customers, Walmart is leaning into the idea. To get started, users open the Muse app, sign in to their Walmart account, and return to the assistant to begin shopping. They can ask it to find specific products, compare options, or track down deals. Once a customer makes a request in Muse, the assistant sends it to Walmart, which returns relevant products and helps build a shopping cart. Walmart says it has built privacy protections into the experience. For instance, Muse doesn’t get access to a customer’s Walmart shopping history or other personal information. Shoppers can also set spending limits, require approval before purchases, and review orders placed by the agent. Plus, the company notes users can always delete their agent’s profile if they want to.

items.content: As AI assistants evolve into more capable agents that can access our files, emails, calendar, browser, and more, the amount of trust we’re expected to place in AI companies is growing. The idea of trust is Maple’s larger theme, as the startup proposes that there’s a way to build an AI app where consumers don’t have to trade privacy for convenience, as its competitors often require with their invasive privacy policies and data collection practices , and sometimes even training on users’ personal data . Instead of asking users to trust that Maple won’t misuse their personal data, it’s attempting to build a business where it can’t access that data in the first place. items.content: Anthropic’s stock fell below its IPO price of $83 , trading as low as $76 a share by midday Tuesday, down nearly 12% from Monday’s close. Falling below the IPO price is often seen as a negative signal because underwriters typically price offerings at a discount to their expected trading value. The AI industry has been eagerly watching how Anthropic’s shares trade, with VCs and other observers saying its performance could serve as a barometer for how public market investors value the sector. The dramatic slump comes less than a week after Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq at $111.50 a share . If its shares continue to trade poorly in the coming weeks, the slide could put pressure on private startup valuations and weaken IPO prospects for other AI companies. Anthropic isn’t the only AI stock selling off on Tuesday. items.title: Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming
items.description: The company said it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated.
items.author: Ivan Mehta
items.content: Music streaming service Tidal said on Tuesday that it will start banning and removing songs generated fully with AI in a bid to stem the flood of submissions to its platform. The company said that over the past 90 days, more than 43% of tracks uploaded to its platform were generated by AI, and that was a major reason driving this decision. Tidal said it will start removing fully AI-generated music on December 9, and the process will result in more than 29 million songs being deleted from the platform by the end of the year. With the new rules in place, the platform said it will be rejecting roughly 80,000-85,000 tracks per day. Tidal is also banning distribution services from delivering 100% AI-generated tracks, and will reject submissions if songs’ metadata says they are made fully using AI. The company said it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated. The move comes as AI-generated music inundates streaming services across the board. Tidal is one of the first major platforms after Bandcamp to ban AI music outright . Deezer, which also provides detection tools to other streaming services , said that it will introduce a toggle to let users filter out AI music . Larger platforms like Spotify and YouTube Music have adopted a milder approach to this issue, choosing to label AI-generated music instead of offering filters or taking stronger measures. items.description: PLUS: Nothing to launch its AI mystery product
items.content: Good morning, tech enthusiasts. Hackers spent the past few weeks breaking into banks, crypto platforms, and even supermarket fridges, some with the help of AI. Now the industry is consolidating to fight back, with CrowdStrike buying Zscaler for $43.9B in the biggest cybersecurity deal ever, aimed at protecting every device and connection under one roof. The Rundown: CrowdStrike is paying $43.9B in stock for Zscaler — the largest cybersecurity deal on record — to put the software guarding corporate laptops and the service screening their traffic under one company. CrowdStrike sells endpoint security — the software guarding laptops and phones. Zscaler sells cloud services that replace VPNs and screen traffic for threats. CEO George Kurtz says the deal opens a path to “the largest AI safety and security company the world has ever seen.” Cost cuts are pegged at $500M a year within 18–24 months of closing, with another ~$1B a year in added revenue projected inside 30 months.
